feedback: Decision: revise. The candidate is the iteration 7 design (kp 3.5, kd 0.8, base_speed 1.6, sensors y = 0.07, x = -0.04 to +0.04, sensor_size 0.012, line_loss last_direction). Iteration 7 is already the best raced design at 304.77. Racing an identical build would reproduce that known result and add no telemetry, so the iteration would gain nothing. There is enough budget for one revise round (review, revision, review, race) before the race, so I use it to test one new lever. Evidence: kd 0.3 to 0.5 gave about +1.5 points, and kd 0.5 to 0.8 (with kp 3.5) lifted the score from 64.17 to 304.77, mostly through oval finishes (13 of 20). Steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom is still 0.23 to 0.25 at kd 0.8, and those tracks still fail. The kp 3.0 test (iteration 8) lowered the score to 296.66 without clearing the bends, so kp is not the lever to push. Keep kp 3.5 and geometry unchanged, and raise kd. If the revised candidate scores at or above 304.77 with more s-bend or slalom progress, approve it. If it scores below 304.77 or oval finishes fall below 13 of 20, the derivative is past its useful range, so approve the kd 0.8 build (iteration 7) instead.
requested_changes: Set controller.kd from 0.8 to 1.0 and keep controller.kp 3.5, sensor y 0.07, base_speed 1.6 and line_loss last_direction. Iteration 4 to 7 showed kd gains, and s-bend and slalom steering_oscillation (0.23 to 0.25 at kd 0.8) is the remaining failure signal, so this tests whether more damping reduces it without losing oval finishes.
If the kd 1.0 revision scores below 304.77 or the oval finishes fall below 13 of 20, return to the iteration 7 build (kd 0.8, kp 3.5) and approve it, since kd 0.8 is the best measured point.

Hold base_speed and geometry fixed in this round. If the revised candidate stays on track on all three tracks but misses the 3.0 s limit, raise base_speed from 1.6 toward 1.8 in a later iteration, not in this one.
